title: EXEC SQL DECLARE CURSOR / OPEN / FETCH / CLOSE — server-side cursor for row-by-row streaming
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CURSOR-LOOP.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  SQLCODE   PIC S9(9) COMP.
       01  WS-NAME   PIC X(30).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           EXEC SQL
              DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR
                 SELECT NAME FROM CUSTOMERS WHERE STATUS = 'A'
           END-EXEC.
           EXEC SQL OPEN C1 END-EXEC.
      *> SQLCODE = +100 signals 'no more rows'.
       FETCH-LOOP.
           EXEC SQL FETCH C1 INTO :WS-NAME END-EXEC.
           IF SQLCODE = 100
              EXEC SQL CLOSE C1 END-EXEC
              STOP RUN
           END-IF.
           DISPLAY WS-NAME.
           GO TO FETCH-LOOP.
notes: Cursor loops are the COBOL streaming pattern for large result sets. Java's ResultSet maps cleanly. The spec must capture the SQLCODE=100 exit condition AND the WHERE-clause invariant so the rewrite's stream filter matches.
